events.summary: Solid first-cut draft with high confidence on taxonomy, origin, reproduction biology, size, edibility/toxicity, and the 'not a tree' framing. Bat pollination in wild relatives is well-sourced; wildlife value in Florida cultivation is appropriately hedged. The Opogona sacchari moth host record is from the Florida State Collection of Arthropods and is accurately framed as a pest association. Invasive status: Musa × paradisiaca does not appear on the FISC list or UF/IFAS invasive assessment as a problem species — watch_invasive set to false with reasonable confidence.

events.feedback:
The draft for the Plantain (Musa × paradisiaca) is in phenomenal shape. It does a fantastic job of highlighting the botanical reality that this "tree" is actually a giant herb, and the inclusion of the nomenclature history with Linnaeus adds a wonderful, high-intellect layer to the page.

To keep up the elite, rigorous standard of your digital signage, we need to address some heavy text duplication between sections and reshape the "What to Look For" block into a high-utility, field-ready guide.

🛠️ Recommended Changes
1. Eliminate Heavy Text Duplication (High Priority)
Right now, your ⚡ QUICK HITS and 🔍 MORE INFORMATION sections are repeating the exact same botanical data almost word-for-word.

The Repeats: The definition of a pseudostem (overlapping leaf sheaths over a hidden rhizome/corm), the "fruit once and die back" life cycle, and the history of Linnaeus's naming mix-up (Musa paradisiaca) are written out nearly identically in both blocks.

The Fix: Keep ⚡ QUICK HITS as your snapp
